data.text/markdown:
Jev lab

Jev is a decision model: it never writes prose. You hand it a state (the facts) and typed questions (yes/no, pick one, score 0-1). It returns an answer with a confidence in about a second. Ordinary code then turns those answers into an outcome with a fixed, versioned policy, so every decision can be replayed and audited. That split (fuzzy judgement by Jev, hard rules in code) is what makes it usable for Mark's "explainable edge" bar.

Where Jev fits in the spike short

The short makes money when the opening spike fades and loses when it keeps running. Jev's job is never to predict price. It answers the judgement questions around the price rule, each one a small, versioned decision we can test on its own and switch off if it doesn't help. The L-numbers match the levels you can browse above.Concrete starting points from the recorded set: level 2 Headline triage and Which 8-K item is this? (catalyst labels), level 3 Catalyst quality grade and Earnings quality (red/yellow/green), level 8 Auditor change in the 8-K and going-concern doubt (Mark's filing-keyword idea), level 13 Earnings gaps (kill switch). The First-Hour Desk shows the same idea end to end on a stand-in breakout strategy. To test any of these on the short: run the decision on the pre-open news for each of the ~575 lab trades, then compare profit factor and tail losers with and without the veto, on tune and holdout separately. That needs a live Jev key; nothing here calls Jev.
